def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangia.physical_scope: The action functional of the framework's force branch with a declared potential presentation: the kinetic energy of the labels in an inertial frame, the mechanical Lagrangian K - U of the presentation, the open chart and the action integral over C^2 curves with fixed endpoints, the first variation and stationarity, and the dimensions of these objects. The item defines model-derived objects only: it asserts no equation of motion, no conservation law, no minimisation property and no empirical value, and it does not claim that any apparatus is described by a Lagrangian or by the potential branch.

def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangia:
## Definition

Adopt one force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: $N\ge1$ particle labels
with fixed masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$ (clause (i)), an open nondegenerate time
window $I_{0}\subseteq\mathbb R$, an open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$
and a force map $F$ with the standing continuity and state-local-Lipschitz
hypotheses of clause (iii) of that postulate. Fix one inertial frame with adapted
coordinates $(t,x)$ and identify position tuples with points of
$\mathbb R^{3N}=(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]]); dimensions are
read by [[def-cm01-units]], inner products and norms are Euclidean
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), and differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. Let $\mathsf M$ be the mass
operator of clause (d) of [[def-cm01-configuration]],
$\mathsf M(x_{1},\dots,x_{N})=(m_{1}x_{1},\dots,m_{N}x_{N})$, a symmetric
positive definite linear map of $\mathbb R^{3N}$.

**(a) Kinetic energy.** The **kinetic energy** of the labels at coordinate
velocity $v\in(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}=\mathbb R^{3N}$ is

$$K(v):=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^{N}m_{i}\,\lvert v_{i}\rvert_{2}^{2}=\frac12\,v\cdot\mathsf M v .$$

$K$ is the restriction of a $C^{\infty}$ function of $(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$ and has
dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ (energy). Its Euclidean gradient is
$K'(v)=\mathsf M v$, because $\partial K/\partial v_{i}=m_{i}v_{i}$
([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]).

**(b) Mechanical Lagrangian of a potential presentation.** Let $(U,d)$ be a
potential presentation of the model's force map in the sense of clause (a) of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]: a function
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{2}$ with dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ and residual forces $d=(d_{1},\dots,d_{N})$ such that
$$F_{i}(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)+d_{i}(t,x,v)$$
on the state domain. The **mechanical Lagrangian of the presentation** is

$$L:I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad L(t,x,v):=K(v)-U(t,x).$$

$L$ is of class $C^{2}$ on its open domain and has dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.
When $d\equiv0$ the presentation is a global potential model and $L$ is a
Lagrangian of the model itself; when $d\not\equiv0$, $L$ carries the potential
part only and the residual forces enter through generalized forces. The
potential representative is part of the declared data: replacing $U$ by
$U+c(t)$ for differentiable $c:I_{0}\to\mathbb R$ replaces $L$ by $L-c(t)$
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (c)).

**(c) Action, variations, stationarity.** Let $a<b$ be reals with
$[a,b]\subseteq I_{0}$ and put $O:=I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$. The set
$O$ is open and contains $[a,b]\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$, so with $n:=3N$
the pair $(O,L)$ is a time-dependent Lagrangian chart over $[a,b]\times Q$ in
the sense of [[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]]. **Admissible
curves** (the $C^{2}$ curves $x:[a,b]\to Q$ with the extension convention of
that definition), **variations** $\eta$ with $\eta(a)=\eta(b)=0$, the
**action**

$$S(x):=\int_{a}^{b}L\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)\,dt,$$

the **first variation** $\delta S(x)[\eta]$ and **stationarity** of $x$ are the
notions of [[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]] instantiated at this
chart; the derivative $x'$ is the coordinate velocity ([[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]]).
The action has dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (energy multiplied by time).
Write $E_{L}(x):[a,b]\to\mathbb R^{3N}$ for the Euler-Lagrange expression of
the instantiated chart.

**(d) Status.** This item defines the action functional and the Lagrangian of a
presentation from data already adopted in the model: no new force law, no
equation of motion and no measured value are introduced. The first variation
of $S$ exists for every admissible curve and variation and its formula, the
equivalence of stationarity with the vanishing of $E_{L}(x)$, and the relation
of both to the model's equation of motion are theorems of this page, not part
of the definition.

pthm-cm07-first-variation-and-euler-lagr.physical_scope: The first variation of the action of a force model with a declared potential presentation, computed in the inertial chart: for every C^2 admissible curve and fixed-endpoint variation the variation exists and equals the integral of minus the potential gradient paired with the variation plus the mass-operator pairing of velocity with the variation's derivative, and the Euler-Lagrange expression of the mechanical Lagrangian is minus the sum of the mass-operator acceleration and the potential gradient. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared potential presentation and the cited mathematical first-variation formula; it asserts no equation of motion, which is the subject of the following items.

pthm-cm07-first-variation-and-euler-lagr:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and the mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$, time
window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and a potential
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{2}$
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]], [[def-cm01-configuration]]).
Let $a<b$ with $[a,b]\subseteq I_{0}$, let $x:[a,b]\to Q$ be a $C^{2}$
admissible curve and let $\eta$ be a variation of $x$
([[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]]). Then:

1. $x+\varepsilon\eta$ is an admissible curve for every sufficiently small
   $|\varepsilon|$, the function $\varepsilon\mapsto S(x+\varepsilon\eta)$ is
   differentiable at $\varepsilon=0$, and

$$\delta S(x)[\eta]=\int_{a}^{b}\Bigl[-\nabla_{x}U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)\cdot\eta(t)+\mathsf M x'(t)\cdot\eta'(t)\Bigr]dt,$$

   where $\nabla_{x}U=(\nabla_{x_{1}}U,\dots,\nabla_{x_{N}}U)$ is the Euclidean
   gradient in the configuration slot and the dot is the Euclidean inner
   product of $\mathbb R^{3N}$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]);

2. the Euler-Lagrange expression of $L$ along $x$ is

$$E_{L}(x)(t)=-\Bigl(\mathsf M x''(t)+\nabla_{x}U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)\Bigr)\qquad(t\in[a,b]).$$

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch and on the declared
potential presentation; it selects no equation of motion and asserts no
empirical value.

pthm-cm07-euler-lagrange-equations.physical_scope: The Euler-Lagrange equation of the mechanical Lagrangian of a declared potential presentation: for a C^2 curve of the model on a fixed interval, stationarity of the action, the vanishing of the Euler-Lagrange expression and the pointwise equation mass-operator acceleration equals minus the potential gradient are equivalent. The equivalence identifies the variational critical-point condition with the model's equation of motion on the interval; it is conditional on the adopted force branch and the declared presentation, and it asserts no solution existence, no minimisation and no empirical content.

pthm-cm07-euler-lagrange-equations:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and the mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $C^{2}$ potential
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]).
Let $a<b$ with $[a,b]\subseteq I_{0}$, and let $x:[a,b]\to Q$ be a $C^{2}$
admissible curve ([[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]]). Then the
following three conditions are equivalent:

1. $x$ is stationary for the action $S$ of $L$;
2. $E_{L}(x)(t)=0$ for every $t\in[a,b]$;
3. $\mathsf M x''(t)=-\nabla_{x}U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)$ for every $t\in[a,b]$.

Condition 3 is the model's equation of motion of the potential branch
([[post-cm02-force-superposition]] clause (iv)) written along the curve for the
presentation $(U,d)$ with the potential part alone: the residual forces $d$ do
not appear, and the statement is therefore a statement about the potential
part of the force map. No existence of curves satisfying these conditions is
asserted.

pthm-cm07-newton-equivalence.physical_scope: The stationary-action principle for the global potential branch of the force model: every motion of the model restricts to a stationary curve of the mechanical action on each closed subinterval, and conversely every C^2 stationary curve on a closed interval is the restriction of the unique maximal motion of the model through its initial datum, so that the stationary curves are exactly the restrictions of motions. The equivalence is conditional on the adopted force branch, on the declared potential presentation with no residual forces, and on the cited existence, uniqueness and continuation theorems; it asserts no global existence, no minimisation property and no empirical statement.

pthm-cm07-newton-equivalence:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $C^{2}$ potential
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]).
Assume the presentation has **no residual forces**, $d\equiv0$, so that the
force map itself is $F_{i}(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)$. Then:

1. **motions are stationary.** If $x:J\to Q$ is a motion of the model on an
   interval $J$ with nonempty interior ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]) and
   $a<b$ with $[a,b]\subseteq J\cap I_{0}$, then the restriction $x|_{[a,b]}$
   is stationary for the action $S$ on $[a,b]$.

2. **stationary curves are restrictions of motions.** If $a<b$ with
   $[a,b]\subseteq I_{0}$ and $x:[a,b]\to Q$ is a $C^{2}$ admissible curve that
   is stationary for $S$, then $x$ is the restriction to $[a,b]$ of the
   maximal motion of the model through the initial datum
   $\bigl(a,x(a),x'(a)\bigr)$ (whose existence and uniqueness are
   [[pthm-cm02-ivp]] clause 4); in particular the maximal interval of that
   motion contains $[a,b]$.

3. **identification.** Consequently the $C^{2}$ curves $x:[a,b]\to Q$ that are
   stationary for the action are exactly the restrictions to $[a,b]$ of the
   motions of the model whose maximal interval contains $[a,b]$, and the model
   equation satisfied is $\mathsf M x''=-\nabla_{x}U$ on that interval.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch and on the declared
potential presentation with $d\equiv0$; it asserts no existence of stationary
curves for arbitrary endpoint data, no minimisation and no empirical value.

pthm-cm07-coordinate-covariance-of-the-e.physical_scope: Covariance of the model's equation of motion under a time-dependent coordinate map of the configuration domain: along a curve described by a C^3 map X with everywhere invertible configuration Jacobian, the Euler-Lagrange expression of the substituted Lagrangian is the transpose-Jacobian multiple of the inertial-chart expression, so the model's potential-part equation holds along the Cartesian description if and only if the substituted Euler-Lagrange equation holds along the coordinate description; when the chart condition holds, this is equivalent to stationarity of the substituted action. The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the potential presentation and the smooth invertibility of the coordinate map; it asserts nothing about constraints with fewer coordinates, which are treated separately, and no empirical claim.

pthm-cm07-coordinate-covariance-of-the-e:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $C^{2}$ potential
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]).
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ be open and nonempty and let
$X:\Omega\to Q$ be of class $C^{3}$ with $X_{q}(t,q)$ invertible for every
$(t,q)\in\Omega$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]],
[[def-invertible-euclidean-linear-map]]). Put

$$\widetilde O:=\bigl\{(t,q,v)\in\Omega\times\mathbb R^{3N}:\ \bigl(t,X(t,q),X_{t}(t,q)+X_{q}(t,q)v\bigr)\in I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}\bigr\},$$

$$\widetilde L(t,q,v):=L\bigl(t,X(t,q),\,X_{t}(t,q)+X_{q}(t,q)v\bigr).$$

Let $a<b$ and let $q:[a,b]\to\mathbb R^{3N}$ be a $C^{2}$ curve with
$(t,q(t),q'(t))\in\widetilde O$ for all $t\in[a,b]$; put $x(t):=X(t,q(t))$.
Then:

1. $\widetilde O$ is open, $\widetilde L$ is of class $C^{2}$ on it, and

$$E_{\widetilde L}(q)(t)=X_{q}\bigl(t,q(t)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}E_{L}(x)(t)\qquad(t\in[a,b]);$$

   consequently $E_{\widetilde L}(q)=0$ on $[a,b]$ if and only if
   $E_{L}(x)=0$ on $[a,b]$, and (by [[pthm-cm07-euler-lagrange-equations]])
   $q$ satisfies the substituted Euler-Lagrange equation if and only if the
   Cartesian description $x$ satisfies the model's potential-part equation
   $\mathsf M x''(t)=-\nabla_{x}U(t,x(t))$ on $[a,b]$.

2. If in addition there is an open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ with
   $q([a,b])\subseteq U$ and $[a,b]\times U\times\mathbb R^{3N}\subseteq\widetilde O$,
   then $(\widetilde O,\widetilde L)$ is a time-dependent Lagrangian chart over
   $[a,b]\times U$ and: $q$ is stationary for the substituted action
   $\widetilde S(q)=\int_{a}^{b}\widetilde L(t,q,q')\,dt$ if and only if $x$ is
   stationary for $S$.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, on the declared
potential presentation and on the smooth invertibility of $X$; the residual
forces $d$ do not enter, so clause 1 concerns the potential part of the force
map.

pthm-cm07-boundary-terms-and-gauge.physical_scope: Gauge properties of the mechanical action of a declared potential presentation: adding to the Lagrangian the total time derivative of a C^3 function defined on the chart time-configuration domain changes the action by endpoint values only and leaves the Euler-Lagrange expression, the stationary curves and the model's stationary-action equation unchanged; changing the potential representative by a function of time alone is an instance and shifts the action by a constant-free endpoint term; multiplying the Lagrangian by a nonzero constant leaves the stationary curves unchanged. The statements are conditional on the adopted force branch and presentation and assert no minimisation and no empirical content.

pthm-cm07-boundary-terms-and-gauge:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $C^{2}$ potential
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]).
Let $a<b$ with $[a,b]\subseteq I_{0}$, let
$F:I_0\times Q\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{3}$, and define

$$L'(t,x,v):=L(t,x,v)+F_{t}(t,x)+F_{x}(t,x)\cdot v .$$

Then:

1. $L'$ is $C^{2}$ on $I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$, has the same
   dimension as $L$, and for every $C^{2}$ admissible curve $x:[a,b]\to Q$ one
   has $E_{L'}(x)(t)=E_{L}(x)(t)$ for all $t\in[a,b]$ and

$$S'(x)=S(x)+F\bigl(b,x(b)\bigr)-F\bigl(a,x(a)\bigr),$$

   where $S'$ is the action of $L'$; consequently $x$ is stationary for $S'$
   if and only if $x$ is stationary for $S$, and, by
   [[pthm-cm07-euler-lagrange-equations]], both are equivalent to the model's
   potential-part equation $\mathsf M x''=-\nabla_{x}U$ along $x$.

2. **Potential representative.** Let $c:I_{0}\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^2$
   with antiderivative $C$ (i.e. $C'=c$), and let $\widetilde U:=U+c$ be the
   representative of [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (c),
   with Lagrangian $\widetilde L=K-\widetilde U$. Then
   $\widetilde L=L+M$ where $M(t,x,v)=F_{t}+F_{x}\cdot v$ for
   $F(t,x):=-C(t)$, so clause 1 applies: the actions of $L$ and
   $\widetilde L$ differ by $C(a)-C(b)$, independently of the curve, and the
   stationary curves and the model's equation are unchanged.

3. **Scaling.** For every real $\lambda\ne0$ one has
   $E_{\lambda L}(x)=\lambda E_{L}(x)$ pointwise, so the stationary curves of
   the Lagrangian $\lambda L$ coincide with those of $L$; the value $\lambda=0$
   is excluded because the zero Lagrangian has every curve stationary.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch and presentation; it
asserts no minimisation, no conservation law and no empirical content, and it
does not remove the need to declare which representative and normalisation are
used by an energy statement.

def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-for.physical_scope: The dictionary from the model's Cartesian description to generalized coordinates: a C^3 configuraton map that is an immersion (a chart when the coordinate count equals 3N, a parametrisation of a regular holonomic-constraint locus when it does not), the substituted Lagrangian with its kinetic metric, the generalized force of a declared force contribution as the Jacobian-transpose multiple, and the declared Lagrange equations with residual generalized forces. The item defines objects and a model class only; it asserts no equivalence with the constrained equation of motion, which is the reduction theorem of this page, and no empirical claim.

def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-for:
## Definition

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $C^{2}$ potential
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]).
Dimensions are read by [[def-cm01-units]]; gradients and Jacobians are those of
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]], transposes those of
[[def-transpose-of-a-matrix]], and $C^{r}$ classes those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) Generalized-coordinate map.** Let $r\ge1$ and let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{r}$ be open and nonempty. A **generalized-coordinate
map of the model** is a map $X:\Omega\to Q$ of class $C^{3}$ whose derivative
$DX(q)$ is injective for every $q\in\Omega$
([[def-euclidean-submersions-and-immersions]]: an immersion); the coordinates
$q=(q_{1},\dots,q_{r})$ each carry a declared dimension $\gamma_{i}$ and unit
fixed as part of the model declaration. The two intended cases are:
$r=3N$ with $DX(q)$ invertible for every $q$ — a **chart** of the configuration
domain — and $r=3N-k$ for an integer $k$ with $1\le k\le3N-1$ with $X$ a
**parametrization** of a regular holonomic-constraint locus as in clause (d).
The **admissible coordinate curves** are the $C^{2}$ maps $q:J\to\Omega$ on an
interval $J\subseteq I_{0}$ with nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]); each such
curve induces the configuration curve $x:=X\circ q:J\to Q$.

**(b) Substituted Lagrangian and kinetic metric.** For a generalized-coordinate
map $X$ define

$$\widetilde L:I_{0}\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad \widetilde L(t,q,v):=L\bigl(t,X(q),DX(q)v\bigr)=\tfrac12\,v^{\mathsf T}G(q)v-\widetilde U(t,q),$$

with the **kinetic metric** and the substituted potential

$$G(q):=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q),\qquad \widetilde U(t,q):=U\bigl(t,X(q)\bigr).$$

$G(q)$ is symmetric and positive definite, because $DX(q)$ is injective and
$\mathsf M$ is symmetric positive definite
([[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]], [[def-linear-map]],
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]]); its entry
$G_{ij}$ has dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\gamma_{i}^{-1}\gamma_{j}^{-1}$ and the
plane quantity $\frac12v^{\mathsf T}G(q)v$ has dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ for every choice of coordinate dimensions.
$\widetilde L$ is of class $C^{2}$; the **substituted action** of an admissible
coordinate curve $q:[a,b]\to\Omega$ with $[a,b]\subseteq I_{0}$ is
$\widetilde S(q):=\int_{a}^{b}\widetilde L(t,q(t),q'(t))dt$ whenever the
chart conventions of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] apply to
$\widetilde L$, and the **Lagrange operator** of $\widetilde L$ is

$$\Lambda(\widetilde L)(q)(t):=\frac{d}{dt}\Bigl(\frac{\partial\widetilde L}{\partial v}\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr)\Bigr)-\frac{\partial\widetilde L}{\partial q}\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr)\in\mathbb R^{r}.$$

**(c) Generalized forces.** Let $f:I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}\to\mathbb R^{3N}$
be a force field of the model's standing regularity
([[post-cm02-force-superposition]] clause (iii)) — for instance the residual
force $d$ of the presentation, or the model's full force map $F$. Its
**generalized force** in the coordinates $X$ is

$$Q_{f}(t,q,v):=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}f\bigl(t,X(q),DX(q)v\bigr)\in\mathbb R^{r};$$

its $i$-th component has the dimension of energy per unit of the coordinate
$q_{i}$, namely $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}\gamma_{i}^{-1}$: the Jacobian factor
$\partial X_{a}/\partial q_{i}$ carries the dimension $\ell\gamma_{i}^{-1}$ and
the force $f_{a}$ the dimension $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$. Thus $Q_{f}\cdot\delta q$
has energy dimension; for a length-valued coordinate $Q_{f,i}$ has force
dimension, and for a dimensionless angle it has torque dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$. For the presentation
$(U,d)$ write $Q^{\mathrm{res}}:=Q_{d}$ for the generalized force of the
residual part; when $d\equiv0$ one has $Q^{\mathrm{res}}\equiv0$.

**(d) Constraint parametrizations.** Let a regular holonomic-constraint datum
$(O,k,G)$ of [[def-cm06-holonomic-constraint-model]] be given, with
time-independent locus $N\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$, i.e.
$\Sigma=\{(t,x)\in O:x\in N\}$ (the scleronomic case). A
**parametrization of the constrained configurations** is a generalized-coordinate
map $X:\Omega\to Q$ with $r=3N-k$, $X(\Omega)=N\cap Q$, and
$(t,X(q))\in O$ for all $(t,q)\in I_{0}\times\Omega$; such a map presents every
constrained configuration exactly once and every admissible coordinate curve
induces a constrained curve family with permitted velocity (proved by the
reduction theorem of this page, which also identifies the virtual
displacements with the image of $DX$).

**(e) Declared Lagrange equations.** With the data of clauses (a)-(c), the
model with presentation $(U,d)$ **declares as its Lagrange equations in the
coordinates $X$**

$$\Lambda(\widetilde L)(q)(t)=Q^{\mathrm{res}}\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr)\qquad(t\in J),$$

posed for $C^{2}$ admissible coordinate curves $q:J\to\Omega$. These equations
are part of the coordinate description: for $d\equiv0$ they reduce to the
Euler-Lagrange equation $\Lambda(\widetilde L)(q)=0$ of the substituted
Lagrangian, and for a chart they are the coordinate form of the model's
equation of motion, as the covariance theorem of this page records. Whether
the same equations describe an ideal constrained motion for a
parametrization of clause (d) is a separate statement, proved as the reduction
theorem of this page; it is not part of this definition.

**(f) Status.** This item defines the dictionary between the Cartesian and the
generalized-coordinate descriptions: the coordinate map, the substituted
Lagrangian, the kinetic metric, generalized forces and the declared Lagrange
equations. It adopts no force law beyond the model's presentation, asserts no
solution existence and makes no empirical claim; the equivalence of the
declared equations with the model's Cartesian equation (for charts) and with
the ideal constrained equation (for parametrizations) is proved on this page.
lem-cm07-immersion-euler-lagrange-transp:
## Statement

Let $n,m\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{n}$ be open and nonempty, and let
$X:\Omega\to\mathbb R^{m}$ be of class $C^{3}$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an
open interval and let $L:J\times\mathbb R^{m}\times\mathbb R^{m}\to\mathbb R$
be of class $C^{2}$, with gradients $L_{x}$ and $L_{w}$ in the second and third
slots ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]],
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Define

$$\widetilde L:J\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^{n}\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad \widetilde L(t,q,v):=L\bigl(t,X(q),DX(q)v\bigr).$$

Then $\widetilde L$ is of class $C^{2}$, and for every interval $J'\subseteq J$
with nonempty interior and every $C^{2}$ curve $q:J'\to\Omega$
([[def-interval]], [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]) with
$x:=X\circ q$ one has, writing $\widetilde L_{q}$ and $\widetilde L_{v}$ for the
gradients of $\widetilde L$ in the second and third slots,

$$\widetilde L_{q}\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr)-\frac{d}{dt}\Bigl(\widetilde L_{v}\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr)\Bigr)=DX\bigl(q(t)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}\Bigl(L_{x}\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)-\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(L_{w}(t,x(t),x'(t))\bigr)\Bigr)$$

for every $t\in J'$. In words: the Euler-Lagrange expression of the
substituted Lagrangian is the transpose-Jacobian multiple of the
Euler-Lagrange expression of the ambient Lagrangian. No invertibility of
$DX$ is assumed; the identity holds for every immersion, and in particular for
square and non-square parameterizations.

pthm-cm07-lagrangian-reduction-of-ideal-.physical_scope: The elimination of ideal scleronomic holonomic constraints by parametrization: for a global C^3 parametrization of the constrained configurations of a scleronomic regular holonomic datum, a C^2 coordinate curve describes an ideal constrained motion of the force model exactly when it solves the declared Lagrange equations of the substituted Lagrangian with the residual generalized force; the reaction is then uniquely determined, annihilates the virtual displacements and admits the unique continuous multiplier. The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the potential presentation, the constraint datum with its rank hypothesis and the ideal-reaction law; it asserts no solution existence, no uniqueness of the coordinate curve for given data and no empirical claim.

pthm-cm07-lagrangian-reduction-of-ideal-:
## Statement

Adopt the force-branch data of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: $N\ge1$
labelled particles with masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, an open time window
$I_{0}$, an open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ and a force map
$F$ with the standing regularity; adopt a regular holonomic-constraint datum
$(O,k,G)$ of [[def-cm06-holonomic-constraint-model]] and the ideal-reaction law
of [[post-cm06-ideal-reaction-law]]. Assume the datum is **scleronomic with
time-independent locus** $N\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$:

$$\Sigma=\bigl\{(t,x)\in O:\ x\in N\bigr\}.$$

Let $(U,d)$ be a potential presentation of $F$ in the sense of clause (a) of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]], so that
$F_{i}(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)+d_{i}(t,x,v)$. Let $r:=3N-k$,
let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{r}$ be open and nonempty, and let
$X:\Omega\to Q$ be a **parametrization of the constrained configurations** in
the sense of clause (d) of [[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]]:
$X$ is of class $C^{3}$, $DX(q)$ is injective for every $q\in\Omega$,
$X(\Omega)=N\cap Q$ and $(t,X(q))\in O$ for all $(t,q)\in I_{0}\times\Omega$.
Define the kinetic metric, substituted potential, substituted Lagrangian and
residual generalized force

$$G(q):=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q),\qquad \widetilde U(t,q):=U\bigl(t,X(q)\bigr),\qquad \widetilde L(t,q,v):=\tfrac12\,v^{\mathsf T}G(q)v-\widetilde U(t,q),$$

$$Q^{\mathrm{res}}(t,q,v):=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}d\bigl(t,X(q),DX(q)v\bigr).$$

Let $J\subseteq I_{0}$ be an interval with nonempty interior, let $q:J\to\Omega$
be a $C^{2}$ curve and put $x:=X\circ q$. Then the following are equivalent:

1. $x$ is a constrained motion of the model with an ideal reaction field: there
   is a continuous $R:J\to\mathbb R^{3N}$ with
   $\mathsf M x''(t)=F\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)+R(t)$ and
   $R(t)\cdot\delta=0$ for every $t\in J$ and every virtual displacement
   $\delta\in\ker D_{x}G(x(t))$;
2. $\Lambda(\widetilde L)(q)(t)=Q^{\mathrm{res}}\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr)$ for
   every $t\in J$, i.e. the declared Lagrange equations of
   [[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]] hold along $q$.

If these hold, then:

3. the reaction is unique: $R(t)=\mathsf M x''(t)-F(t,x(t),x'(t))$ for every
   $t\in J$, and there is a unique continuous
   $\lambda:J\to\mathbb R^{k}$ with
   $R(t)=D_{x}G(x(t))^{\mathsf T}\lambda(t)$;
4. the virtual displacements at $x(t)$ are exactly the image of $DX(q(t))$,
   $\ker D_{x}G(x(t))=DX(q(t))\bigl(\mathbb R^{r}\bigr)$;
5. the statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the presentation,
   the scleronomic regular constraint datum and the ideal-reaction law. No
   solution existence, no uniqueness of the coordinate curve for given data
   and no empirical content are asserted.

rem-cm07-scope-and-singular-warnings.physical_scope: Scope audit of the stationary-action formulation of the force model: stationarity is not minimisation; the mechanical Lagrangians of this framework are regular and the chart Legendre map is hyperregular, so the second-order equations determine accelerations, while degenerate Lagrangians are excluded; the unrestricted action principle is not available for velocity constraints and is refuted by the cited counterexample; and the stationary-action equivalence is a conditional theorem of the model, not empirical evidence. The remark asserts no new physical claim.

ex-cm07-free-particle-straight-lines.physical_scope: A worked check of the stationary-action equivalence on the free one-label model: zero force map, zero potential, Cartesian Lagrangian of a free particle; on every closed time interval the stationary curves are exactly the affine uniform motions, for each pair of endpoint configurations there is exactly one, and the action difference to the stationary curve is a nonnegative quadratic functional of the variation, so the stationary curve is a minimiser within the fixed-endpoint class. All quantities are model values under the declared idealization of a particle subject to no force.

ex-cm07-oscillator-stationary-saddle-che.physical_scope: A worked check that stationarity is not minimisation, on the one-dimensional harmonic oscillator model with positive stiffness: on intervals longer than pi divided by the angular frequency, arbitrarily small fixed-endpoint variations around the zero stationary curve produce both strictly larger and strictly smaller actions, so the stationary curve is neither a local minimiser nor a local maximiser; on shorter intervals every sine-mode variation in the checked family increases the action. The computation uses exact model actions and exact trigonometric integrals; no experimental values are reported.

ex-cm07-polar-coordinate-kinetic-metric-.physical_scope: A worked check of the coordinate-covariance theorem on cylindrical coordinates for one labelled particle of mass m in a declared potential presentation: the substituted Lagrangian has kinetic metric m diag(1, r^2, 1), the coordinate Euler-Lagrange equations are exactly the Cartesian equation written in the cylindrical frame, and the Cartesian stationary curves correspond to the coordinate solutions. All quantities are model values under the declared potential; no measurement is reported.

ex-cm07-total-derivative-gauge-check.physical_scope: A worked gauge check on the free one-label model: adding the total time derivative of F(t,x)=alpha*t*x to the free Lagrangian changes the action by the endpoint value alpha(b x(b) - a x(a)) and leaves the Euler-Lagrange expression equal to the original one on every curve, hence leaves the stationary curves and the model's equation of motion unchanged; the potential normalization U + gamma t is the special case F = -gamma*t^2/2. The values are exact model values of a declared computation.

ex-cm07-nonholonomic-unrestricted-action.physical_scope: A worked check on the nonholonomic constraint z' = x y' with unit mass and zero applied force: the d'Alembert motion from the stated initial data has strictly positive y' and nonzero y'' on the positive half-line, so it cannot satisfy the vakonomic (unrestricted-action) equations of the same constraint, which force y'' to vanish wherever x'' does. Consequently the unrestricted action principle is not a substitute for the d'Alembert prescription on this branch. The example reports exact model computations, not measurements.

ex-cm07-pendulum-constraint-elimination-.physical_scope: A worked check of the constraint-elimination theorem on the planar pendulum model: one particle of mass m constrained without friction to a circle of radius l in the plane z=0 under a uniform downward field; the parametrization by the angle gives kinetic metric m l^2, substituted potential -m g l cos(theta), the pendulum equation theta-ddot = -(g/l) sin(theta), and the reaction as a normal multiple with the explicit multiplier, so the parametrized solutions are exactly the ideal constrained motions. All quantities are model values of the declared idealization.
